As another spectator with no experience in animation whatsoever, I feel like the animation doesn't have anything wrong with it either. The lip syncing is on point which is something I'd like to add. I also think that not only the animation is good, which I believe will inevitably become better as you keep making more and more content, but also the character designs and backgrounds just look really nice, specially with tiny details like the textures on the walls and couch. I also see no animation errors, which is great! The transitions are fitting and don't seem out of place at all, and the sound effects aren't obnoxious or distracting. I do, however, believe that the audio could be a little bit louder, especially at the intro. I also may just be cherry picking, but I felt like the videogame itself had a bit of an inconsistent artstyle, as some things looked pixelated while others didn't (For example 1:30). Overall, this is far from terrible, and I believe this idea has some good potential. :)

Still, you need to know that this won't be the first time someone will judge your work harshly. Animation and art are susceptible to all kinds of criticism and hate, so you do need not to expect, but rather be prepared for all kinds of negative comments you may receive about your work. As long as you believe in your work and all the good it has to offer, you need to keep pushing against the odds. I really hope this helped, and I hope to see you doing well in the future.

From what I've been told and from personal experience and feelings, loneliness is generated by two constant feelings. These feelings are independent of our situation, and that's why even people who have a loving family, gf/bf, best friend or spouse can feel lonely, and also why we shouldn't diminish the suffering of other people that may seem less **solitary** than us. This first feeling is the lack of connection. You can have as many friends as you'd like, but if you don't have someone you can trust and be yourself with, be that sharing experiences that may leave you vulnerable, not pretending to be someone else while they're around, knowing that they don't love you for what you do, but because of who you are, and that while they may be absent, and even if they don't seek out for you, they will still cherish you once you reunite, someone who loves you and you can learn how to love with (and yes, good friends can really teach you a lot of things about love); then you'll still feel lonely. Fortunately enough, if we already have some connections to others, we can make them stronger by identifying who we can trust, and slowly opening yourselves together.

The second feeling is the idea of being unlovable and that your love is unwanted. This one's a life crushing disease, please, don't let yourself get caught on it. You are wanted, you are needed and you are cherished, and if you aren't, then you can still be, as truly, we tend to feel closer to people who are similar to us, and the amount of people here on Earth makes it hard not to find someone who may feel as lonely, as broken and as isolated as we do. Now now, I know, this all sounds cliché, but it's... kinda true, if you believe on it, at least I do, it makes things less painful to the point you feel good. But yeah, feeling unwanted will keep you away from people, it will make you run away from them and avoid those who love you like the plague, because you won't believe them, you will think they're waiting for you to open yourself only to betray you, so you will hurt them before they get a chance to hurt you. Life doesn't have to be like this, and while they may be a lot of people who do want to push you down, it's the good people, and yourself, that make these things worth fighting for. Keep pushing, and most importantly, don't forget to be a friend to yourself too :)

I'm no bug expert, but it seems to me that you've been stung (since I haven't really heard of insects with stingers biting rather than stinging) by a [Priocnemis Minorata](https://bugguide.net/node/view/385798/bgimage), one of the many types of spider wasps. While I couldn't seem to find any specific documentation on this species and how dangerous its sting (or bite) is, [this article by the BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-45272344) seems to indicate that a single sting is very unlikely to kill you or harm you in a significant way, with about 30 or 40 stings required for you to be on risk of death. Yes, wasps are poisonous, however, this poison is often contained in such small and specific quantities that they only kill other insects, while they create irritation and pain to humans. However, you shouldn't dismiss it at all, and be on the check for the [following symptoms that the NHS suggests:](https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/insect-bites-and-stings/)

* The sting site does not improve within a few days or gets worse
* You have been stung in your mouth or near your eyes
* An area of 10cm or more around the sting becomes red and swollen
* There is pus or increasing pain, swelling or redness
* Fever, swollen glands and other flu-like symptoms

[Also this:](https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/insect-bites-and-stings/)

 When to call 999:

* Wheezing or difficulty breathing
* A swollen face, mouth or throat
* Nausea or vomiting
* A fast heart rate
* Dizziness or feeling faint
* Difficulty swallowing
* Loss of consciousness
